# Page Cache: ICO Guidance on AI-Generated FOI Requests (May 2026)

**Source:** https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/media-centre/news-and-blogs/2026/05/new-guidance-to-support-public-authorities-dealing-with-ai-generated-foi-requests/  
**Mirror:** https://www.publicsectorexecutive.com/articles/new-guidance-public-authorities-dealing-ai-generated-foi-requests  
**Retrieved:** 2026-06-24  
**Relevance:** Directly addresses the operational context our system is designed for; sets the legal and procedural baseline for how public authorities must handle all FOI requests, including those generated by AI tools.

---

## Context

FOI request volumes hit 94,526 in 2025 (up from 83,041 in 2024) — the highest since monitoring began in 2005. The ICO attributes part of this growth to AI-assisted request drafting. Without clear guidance, the ICO warned this "risks placing pressure on FOI teams and could lead to delays, errors or increased complaints."

## Core Legal Principle

**All FOI requests must receive fair and consistent handling regardless of how they were created.** Public authorities remain legally obligated to respond under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. The guidance adds no new legal requirements — it clarifies application of existing law to a new context.

## Key Risks of AI-Generated Requests

AI-drafted FOI requests frequently:
- Misquote or misunderstand FOI legislation
- Contain unclear or confusing wording
- Require significant clarification before processing can begin

## Handling Recommendations for Public Authorities

- Apply existing FOI principles consistently to all submissions
- Use practical wording to encourage responsible AI use by requesters
- Request clarification where ambiguity prevents processing
- Implement consistent internal processes across all request types

## Relevance to Our System (AI Assistants Processing FOI)

The guidance also notes: *"used responsibly, AI also has the potential to help public authorities improve how they handle FOI requests."* This is an explicit ICO acknowledgement that AI on the *processing* side is legitimate — provided it is used responsibly and does not replace human decision-making.

**Implication for our design:** the human approval gate (HITL in `hitl.py`) is not just a rubric requirement — it is the mechanism that keeps the system compliant with this principle.
